title: Map Selection to Source-Style Vector
objective: Click a body location and generate a source-style candidate address under a named frozen profile - the five-token display when representable, else an extended variable-depth packet with the nearest-encodable point and its quantization error.

repository_truth.head: de620bb
reused_engine: cwatlas.r1082.local_coord.inverse (via safe_family_inverse) + wire_format; cwatlas.icosahedron - NOT reimplemented

implementation.extended_packet: self-describing wire packet (SHELL_ONLY | SHELL_PLUS_COARSE | FULL) via wire_format; shell supplies the radius

claims.statement: The inverse geocoder maps a body location (lat, lon, shell) under a named frozen profile to a source-style five-token candidate address, returning the nearest-encodable point with an explicit quantization residual and the other retained families' addresses as aliases.

negative_results: The source codec is quantized: an arbitrary click is generally NOT exactly representable, so the nearest-encodable point and its residual are returned and exactness is not claimed (representable_exact=False). Quantization is shown before the operator copies the vector.
Non-uniqueness is surfaced: under an un-narrowed ensemble different token-order families emit different source vectors for the same click (non_unique=True with the alias set).
The shell supplies the radius; altitude is never reported missing. A named frozen profile is required (a bare inverse with no calibration is refused).
A recovered address is at most a CALIBRATED_CANDIDATE; assert_not_measured() raises. No source origin is validated.
privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic/public coordinates and vectors only; no private path literals, no personal identity tokens, no raw private narrative
